newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies sharply on distillate demand.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies sharply on distillate demand.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures rallied sharply on Thursday as heating oil prices on both sides of the Atlantic pushed further into five-year high territory, brokers said.
Low stock levels, a cold spell in the U.S. Northeast and continued high premiums for prompt physical gas oil supply in Europe helped stoke the buying frenzy in oil futures.

November Brent gained 64 cents to close at $23.71 per barrel while October gas oil jumped $3.50 to $246.00 per tonne. The November Brent-gas oil crack spread ended at $8.00 per barrel, a full $2.00 above where it stood only last Friday.
The October/November gas oil spread jumped another 50 cents to $11.50 per tonne.
A cold spell in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, sparked nervous buying as U.S. distillate stocks stood 29 percent below last year.
"People are looking at the low stock situation and are severly worried about what will happen when winter hits," a broker said.
Meteorologists said heating demand in the U.S. northeast would be above normal in the next few days as temperatures run 5-10 degrees Farenheit below normal.
Europe's physical gas oil traders were paying up to $20.00 per tonne premium to November futures for a cargo of low sulphur diesel delivered in the middle of October.
The strength of gas oil in turn supported North Sea crude markets where sweet grades were in most demand.
"Everywhere you look the fundamentals are bullish. Who would want to sell at this stage?" a broker said.
